matches.quote: The proximity-effect and one-dimensional interpretations are presented more strongly than the data allow... recast the section explicitly as a hypothesis, dropping "quantitatively supported"
the 1D wire and the waveguide, which motivate the paper, are not studied by dissipation.
Fig. 4c shows a narrow anomalous dark band next to a high-dissipation sliver near 0 mT... The map is asymmetric (the low-dissipation band is offset toward ≈−10 to −30 mT...
Edge localization, the edge/interior contrast and the width independence are therefore not demonstrated... extend to channels of different widths
The CPD-to-density conversion (Eq. 1) is not reliable enough to place regions on the superconducting dome... treats the LAO as an ideal parallel-plate capacitor (~1.5 nm, ε_r = 25).
only one boundary of the 1 µm 2D channel is mapped... The authors should map Γ(x, y, V) across both edges and the interior of the 2D channel
The text gives Ic = 30 nA for both devices, while Fig. 1e–f for Device A shows peaks at ≈±12 nA at 47 mT and a zero-field diamond tip near ≈20 nA.

Eq. (1) treats the LAO as an ideal parallel-plate capacitor... ignores the tip-induced field, the very large and field-dependent permittivity of STO at mK... quantum capacitance... and the surface charge, dipoles
map Γ(x, y, V) across both edges and the interior of the 2D channel, at several X positions... give the distribution of β/α over many pixels inside and outside
No field map is shown at point B... (ii) repeat the field map of Fig. 4c at point B and over bare STO under identical setpoints
The mechanism by which superconductivity would suppress the measured dissipation is not established for this geometry... Without this, "ΔV⁴ emerges in superconducting regions" is not supported.
compare the written-line width with the measured density profile, and show CPD and dissipation over the 1D wire, which would directly test the one-dimensional claims.

notes: C6 is marked partly because P3 and P4 ask for spatial maps of Gamma(x,y,V) along X and maps/distributions of beta/alpha across the pattern rather than framing it specifically as checking inhomogeneity within the edge channel. C8 is marked partly because P3/P9/P20 note that the 1D wire motivates the paper and is in the transport path yet is never measured by dissipation, whereas the referee asks to explain its relevance to the presented SPM data. C9 is marked partly because P16 critiques the fixed dielectric model in Eq. (1) at 10 mK by focusing on STO permittivity, quantum capacitance, and dipoles rather than the temperature dependence of LAO's dielectric constant.
